metadata.note: The Avon, Geneseo and Mount Morris Railroad (AG&MM) served the Genesee Valley south of Rochester, connecting the villages of Avon, Geneseo, and Mount Morris. (The Mount Morris - Dansville line beyond was a separate company, the Erie and Genesee Valley / Dansville and Mount Morris Railroad, and is drawn in data/dansville_and_mount_morris_railroad.geojson.) Chartered as the Genesee Valley Railroad in 1856, it reached Geneseo and Mount Morris in January 1859, was reorganized as the AG&MM in 1860 after a foreclosure, and was leased to the Erie Railway in 1872 -- eventually becoming the Erie Railroad's 'Mount Morris Branch,' operated in conjunction with the Rochester and Genesee Valley Railroad's line into Rochester. Notably, the Erie fully electrified this branch (Rochester to Mount Morris) in 1906-1907, running it as an hourly electric commuter service until de-electrification began in 1934; passenger service between Rochester and Avon ended September 30 1941, and the line was abandoned in 1940-1941. GEOMETRY NOTE: Rochester-Avon (now in data/erie_rochester_branch.geojson) is real-traced from OpenStreetMap active/abandoned rail tagging. The Mount Morris-Dansville tail formerly drawn here was removed 2026-10-18 (see dansville_split_2026_10). The Avon-Geneseo-Mount Morris core segment is a straight-line approximation instead -- the OSM-tagged track in that stretch resolved to a real, connected path, but one that both backtracked (dipping south past Geneseo's latitude before turning back) and totaled roughly 50% longer than the sourced historic '15 miles' Avon-Mount Morris figure, indicating it traces a different, non-historic modern alignment rather than the original 1859 AG&MM route -- flagged honestly rather than presented as accurate track.

geometry_sources: OpenStreetMap (via Overpass API, overpass.openstreetmap.fr mirror): railway=rail (active) combined with railway=abandoned/disused tagging; routed via Dijkstra shortest path between geocoded station coordinates for Rochester-Avon and (formerly) Mount Morris-Dansville, both of which resolved to plausible, non-backtracking real paths. The Avon-Geneseo-Mount Morris stretch was rejected in favor of a straight-line approximation after its traced path both backtracked and measured ~50% longer than the sourced historic mileage for that stretch. [2026-10-18: the Mount Morris-Dansville trace is no longer part of this file; see dansville_split_2026_10 for why it was wrong.]

metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.
metadata.trim_note: 2026-08-24: this feature previously ran Rochester – Dansville, drawing the Rochester–Avon leg (the Rochester and Genesee Valley Railroad's line, opened 1853) as part of the AG&MM and from 1859, which both attributed it to the wrong company and started it six years late. That leg now lives in data/erie_rochester_branch.geojson, split by operator per Rule 4; this feature was cut back to Avon (its own railroad's actual north end) and relabelled Avon – Dansville. 49 leading vertices removed and replaced with the shared Avon endpoint -77.74880, 42.91243 so the two layers meet.
metadata.dansville_split_2026_10: 2026-10-18: removed the Mount Morris - Dansville tail (15 trailing vertices after the Mount Morris vertex -77.87417, 42.72562, about 14.9 mi) and relabelled the feature 'Avon – Dansville' -> 'Avon – Mount Morris'. Why: (1) the AG&MM never owned or ran Mount Morris - Dansville. It was built 1871-72 by the Erie and Genesee Valley Railroad, run by the Erie under lease 1872 - 21 Oct 1891 and by the independent Dansville and Mount Morris Railroad from 22 Oct 1891 to the end of passenger service in 1939. Drawing it as part of this feature showed it from 1859, 12-13 years before it was built, in the AG&MM colour throughout, and to 1941, two years after its passengers ended. It also drew the 1907-1934 hourly electric service to Dansville, though the wire stopped at Mount Morris. (2) The removed geometry was poor. Mount Morris - Groveland was a single 5.7 mi straight chord, despite the metadata calling it real-traced. Groveland - Dansville was a coarse 9-vertex run along the surviving D&MM stub. Its vertices are identical to those of the DL&W main line in scranton_railroads.geojson, so that layer draws the Lackawanna on D&MM track there: an open defect in that file, not fixed here. The stretch is now drawn in data/dansville_and_mount_morris_railroad.geojson as two features on a fresh OSM trace that starts at this feature's Mount Morris vertex: Erie 1872-1891 and Dansville and Mount Morris 1891-1939. Segment years, colour, company and the Avon - Mount Morris coordinates of this feature are unchanged. Still open, and NOT done here: a Rule 4 split at 1872, when the Erie leased this line (the Erie colour is pulled from erie_rochester_branch.geojson), and the 1941 end, which research puts at 20 Jan 1940 for Avon - Mount Morris. Both are in research/branches/dansville_and_mount_morris_railroad.txt.

De-electrification began in 1934, with gas-electric motor cars replacing the electric equipment. Frequency from real 1907 timetable detail (hourly).
